subject: Priv deploy template harmonization and CI slimdown
messages:
From: Carmen Liu <platformops@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: acme-sec@acme.com
Date: 2028-04-12T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Priv deploy templates & CI alignment for ACME pilot

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. We attached our baseline requirements (see acme-deploy-requirements.pdf) and would like Redwood to review two things before the pilot:

1) A single canonical set of IaC templates (TF modules + Helm charts + Ansible roles) we can adopt, with clear module boundaries so we can keep some ownership internally.
2) A slim CI pattern that works in air-gapped datacenters (artifact signing, offline Helm registries, Ansible artifacts).

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood map which TF modules will be opinionated vs. pluggable?
- Recommended Terraform state backend for on-prem (S3 compatible? DB-backed?).
- How the Helm values overlays will be handled for tenant-specific tweaks.
- CI gating: We need a minimal checklist for preflight tests and an approval flow that integrates with our ticketing.

We also have HSM/KMS constraints and a no-egress policy from the cluster to the public internet. Forwarding to acme-sec on CC for specifics.

Would love a review by EOD Wednesday (PST) and a short design call early Thursday.

Attachments: acme-deploy-requirements.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

Thanks,
Carmen Liu
Senior Platform Engineer — Acme Financial
platformops@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Carmen Liu <platformops@acme.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-12T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy templates & CI alignment for ACME pilot

Hi Carmen —

Thanks for the clear summary and the requirements doc. We've started an internal pass and attached our reference bundle (redwood-priv-deploy-reference-v1.zip) which contains:
- a proposed module layout for Terraform (networking, enclave, control-plane, logging)
- Helm chart overlay strategy (base chart + tenant overlays)
- Ansible role examples for host bootstrap and package installation
- a short CI proposal (priv-ci-proposal-20280412.md) with gating suggestions for air-gapped installs

High-level notes / where we think we should align in the first review:
- Module ownership: Redwood can maintain the control-plane modules; tenant network/egress modules we propose as "customer-owned" with interface contracts.
- State/backends: our recommendation is a customer-managed S3-compatible backend with Dynamo-style locking (consensus lock via Consul or a small lock service). If the customer cannot run this, we can propose a small PostgreSQL-backed state service with row-level locks.
- Artifact handling: charts and binary artifacts can be pushed to a private registry under your network. We include an offline registry bootstrap in the zip.
- Signing: propose artifact signatures (cosign) and manifest checks in CI.

Open questions for the call:
1) Which subnets / VPC boundaries do you strictly control vs. want Redwood to manage?
2) Any existing CMDB / service catalog we need to integrate for inventory?
3) Which approval flow (Jira/ServiceNow) should our canary promotion hooks call?

Propose Thursday 2028-04-13 15:00-15:30 UTC for a 30m alignment. If that works, we'll send a calendar invite and a lightweight agenda.

Attachments: redwood-priv-deploy-reference-v1.zip (archive, 3.4MB); priv-ci-proposal-20280412.md (text)

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Carmen Liu <platformops@acme.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-12T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy templates & CI alignment for ACME pilot

Adding a few technical clarifications from the infra side — quickly summarized so we can have focused decisions on the call: 

- Terraform: break into these modules: networking (VLANs/subnets, route tables), cluster-bootstrap (bastion, bootstrapping nodes), enclave (kube control-plane + autoscaling config), observability (metrics/logging sinks). Each module should export an explicit set of outputs and a narrow input surface. Avoid cross-module implicit state access.

- State backend options:
  * Preferred: customer-run S3-compatible object store + Consul for locks (lightweight, resilient, works air-gapped).
  * Fallback: Postgres-backed remote state with row-locks and a tiny lock daemon. This reduces operational footprint but requires strong backup SLAs.

- Helm: we recommend a two-layer values overlay: base values (kept in TF/helm repo) + runtime overlays generated at deploy time from a small templating engine (ytt or kustomize). Keep secrets out of values and use sealed-secrets / KMS-unseal step in bootstrap.

- Ansible: roles should be idempotent, tightly scoped (ntp, os-hardening, container-runtime). Avoid pushing app manifests from Ansible — let Helm handle that.

- CI gating for air-gapped: minimal flow we can automate: PR -> static lint (tfsec/tflint/helm lint) -> policy check (OPA) -> build & sign artifacts (cosign) -> manual approval -> staged promotion to offline registry. We will produce a small bootstrap script to seed the offline registry and the signed manifest.

Risk flag: bastion egress. If the bastion or the cluster needs to fetch images or updates from public registries, we'll need a controlled egress window or a vendor-approved mirror. Please confirm whether that is possible.

Quoted from Marissa's message: "State/backends: our recommendation is a customer-managed S3-compatible backend with Dynamo-style locking..." — agreed but want to keep the Postgres fallback as documented.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Carmen Liu <platformops@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-sec@acme.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-04-12T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priv deploy templates & CI alignment for ACME pilot

Marissa / Priyom —

Thanks, this is helpful and close to what we expected. A few constraints to call out from security (attaching acme-hsm-specs.pdf):

- HSM/KMS: All signing keys must be backed by our HSM. We cannot ship private keys to Redwood-managed processes. We can provide a signing gateway reachable from the bastion network that performs signing operations.
- No egress: Clusters cannot reach the public internet. Any image pulls must be from an internal mirror. During bootstrap we can allow a restricted pull window (subject to approval) but we'd prefer to avoid that.
- Audit logs: Terraform runs and Helm promotions must produce an immutable audit trail for at least 2 years.

Given that, your offline registry + cosign flow seems fine. For state backend, we will provision an S3-compatible object store and a small Consul cluster for locks (we are comfortable running Consul).

We accept the meeting Thursday 15:00 UTC. For the agenda please include: 1) module ownership & interface contracts; 2) signing + bootstrap pattern; 3) CI gating steps and approval flow integration with our ServiceNow.

Attachments: acme-hsm-specs.pdf (pdf, 450KB)

Regards,
Carmen
